## `README-ru.md`

````markdown
# Tap - библиотека для парсинга CLI на Rust

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/tap-rs.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/tap-rs)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-repo-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/pt-main/tap/tree/rust)
[![Docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tap-rs/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/tap-rs)

```bash
cargo add tap-rs
# OR
cargo add --git https://github.com/pt-main/tap/rs
```

**Tap** - лёгкая библиотека для построения CLI на Rust. Простой API для парсинга аргументов, команд, флагов и цветного вывода. Одна зависимость (`string_template`), без макросов.

---

## Особенности

- Цветной вывод через короткие коды: `[?GN]`, `[?RD]`, `[?YW]` и т.д.
- Автогенерация справки с группировкой команд по одинаковым обработчикам.
- Сабкоманды (вложенные команды).
- Рендереры вывода с шаблонами и типизацией плюс JSON-сериализация.

---

## Быстрый старт

Простое CLI с командой `hello`:

```rust
use tap::{
    argsparsing::ArgsP,
    engine::structs::{CmdInfo, Engine, ErrorType},
    tooling::console::engine::add_help_handler,
};

fn hello_handler(_: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    let name = args.first().unwrap_or(&"World");
    println!("Hello, {}!", name);
    Ok(())
}

fn main() {
    let mut ap = ArgsP::new();
    let mut engine = Engine::new(&mut ap, "MyApp v1.0".to_string());

    engine.new_command(
        "hello",
        CmdInfo::new(hello_handler, vec![], vec!["name"], false, "Say hello"),
    );

    add_help_handler(vec!["help", "-h"], &mut engine);

    if let Err(e) = engine.main() {
        eprintln!("Error: {}", e);
    }
}
```

Запуск:

```bash
$ cargo run hello Rust
Hello, Rust!
$ cargo run hello
Hello, World!
$ cargo run help
MyApp v1.0

╭───────  Command [help OR -h]
⎬─ Args: (none)
⎬─ Docs:
│     Generate and print help message
╰─────── 
╭───────  Command [hello]
⎬─ Args: [name]
⎬─ Docs:
│     Say hello
╰─────── 
```

Символы рамки в выводе `help` - это то, что реально печатает `generate_help`. Не украшение README.

---

## Команды и аргументы

```rust
fn my_handler(e: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType { ... }

engine.new_command(
    "copy",                               // имя команды
    CmdInfo::new(
        my_handler,                       // функция-обработчик
        vec!["src", "dst"],               // обязательные аргументы
        vec!["force"],                    // опциональные
        false,                            // unlimited: если true, принимает любое число доп. аргументов
        "Copy source to destination",     // описание для справки
    ),
);
```

Справка покажет:

```
╭───────  Command [copy]
⎬─ Args: <src>, <dst>, [force]
⎬─ Docs:
│     Copy source to destination
╰─────── 
```

---

## Флаги

Флаги записываются как `--flag`, `--key=value`, `--key:value`. Парсятся автоматически в `ArgsP`:

- `args_p.flags` - список флагов без значений.
- `args_p.values` - словарь ключ -> значение.

Чтение в обработчике:

```rust
fn my_handler(e: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    if e.args_p.flags.contains(&"verbose".to_string()) {
        println!("Verbose mode enabled");
    }
    if let Some(out) = e.args_p.values.get("output") {
        println!("Output file: {}", out);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Важно: флаги вырезаются из `args` до вызова обработчика. Смотрите их только через `e.args_p`.

---

## Цвета

Цветной вывод через коды `[?COLOR]`:

- `[?GN]`, `[?GREEN]` - зелёный
- `[?BGN]`, `[?BGREEN]` - ярко-зелёный
- `[?BACKGREEN]`, `[?BKGN]` - зелёный фон
- `[?BACKBGREEN]`, `[?BKBGN]` - ярко-зелёный фон
- `[?BOLD]`, `[?BD]` - жирный
- `[?DIM]`, `[?DM]` - тусклый
- `[?ITALIC]`, `[?IT]` - курсив
- `[?UNDERLINE]`, `[?UE]` - подчёркнутый
- `[?BLINK]`, `[?BL]` - мигающий
- `[?REVERSE]`, `[?RV]` - инвертированный
- `[?STRIKETHROUGH]`, `[?ST]` - зачёркнутый
- `[?RT]` - сброс

Формат: `[?<BACKGROUND><BRIGHT><COLOR>]`.

- `<BACKGROUND>` - префикс `BK` (кратко) или `BACK` (полностью) для фона. (опциональный)
- `<BRIGHT>` - префикс `B` для яркого варианта. (опциональный)
- `<COLOR>` - имя или две буквы (первая и последняя буква названия). Пример: `GN` = green. (обязательный)

### Палитра

**Стандартные 16**: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white и их яркие варианты. Все доступны как фон.

**Расширенные (xterm-256)**: доступны и как фон:

| Название  | Сокр. | Название    | Сокр. |
|-----------|-------|-------------|-------|
| orange    | `OE`  | lime        | `LE`  |
| pink      | `PK`  | teal        | `TL`  |
| purple    | `PE`  | navy        | `NY`  |
| violet    | `VT`  | gold        | `GD`  |
| brown     | `BN`  | silver      | `SR`  |
| gray      | `GY`  | maroon      | `MN`  |

Примеры: `[?OE]` - оранжевый, `[?BACKGOLD]` / `[?BKGD]` - золотой фон, `[?BKOE]` - оранжевый фон.

### Стили

`BOLD` (`BD`), `DIM`/`FAINT` (`DM`), `ITALIC` (`IT`), `UNDERLINE` (`UE`), `BLINK` (`BL`), `REVERSE` (`RV`), `STRIKETHROUGH` (`ST`), `RESET` (`RT`).

### Использование

```rust
use tap::tooling::colors::print::println;
use tap::tooling::colors::set::colorize;

let raw = "[?GN]Успех![?RT] Файл сохранён как [?YW]config.toml[?RT]";

println(raw);                       // печатает уже раскрашенным
let colored: String = colorize(raw); // или получите строку
```

`println`/`print` в `colors::print` уже вызывают `colorize` внутри - не нужно красить дважды.

Отключить цвета глобально:

```rust
use tap::tooling::colors::set::COLOR_ENABLED;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

COLOR_ENABLED.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
```

Неизвестные коды (`[?FOO]`) не съедаются и не превращаются в мусор - они остаются в строке как есть. Это удобно для отладки.

---

## Группировка команд в справке

Команды с одинаковыми `CmdInfo` автоматически группируются в одну строку как алиасы:

```rust
engine.new_commands(
    vec!["help", "-h"],
    CmdInfo::new(help_handler, vec![], vec![], false, "Show help"),
);
```

В справке будет `[help / -h]`.

Сравниваются `required`, `optional`, `unlimited` и `docs`. Если `docs` отличаются - группировки не будет.

---

## Рендереры

Модуль `tooling::renderable` позволяет шаблонизировать вывод по scope:

```rust
use tap::tooling::renderable::{
    Renderable, add_template_render, add_template_render_colored,
};

let mut r = Renderable::new();
r.scope.insert("name", "Rust");
r.scope.insert("version:int", "1");     // :int - валидируется как число
r.scope.insert("stable:bool", "true");  // :bool - только "true"/"false"

add_template_render("Hello, {{name}} (v{{version}})", "plain", &mut r);
add_template_render_colored("[?GN]Hello, {{name}}[?RT]", "colored", &mut r);

println!("{}", r.render_with("plain").unwrap());
println!("{}", r.render_with("colored").unwrap());
println!("{}", r.render_json().unwrap()); // {"name":"Rust","stable":true,"version":1}
```

`render_json` возвращает `Result` - при невалидном `:int`/`:bool` вернёт `RenderError::InvalidValue`, а не молча вставит мусор в JSON.

---

> MIT - подробности в файле LICENSE.
> 2026, By Pt.
````

## `README.md`

````markdown
# Tap - a CLI parsing library for Rust

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/tap-rs.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/tap-rs)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-repo-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/pt-main/tap/tree/rust)
[![Docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tap-rs/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/tap-rs)

```bash
cargo add tap-rs
# OR
cargo add --git https://github.com/pt-main/tap/rs
```

**Tap** is a lightweight library for building CLIs in Rust. Simple API for parsing arguments, commands, flags, and colored output. One dependency (`string_template`), no macros.

---

## Features

- Colored output via short codes: `[?GN]`, `[?RD]`, `[?YW]`, etc.
- Auto-generated help with grouping of commands by identical handlers.
- Subcommands (nested commands).
- Output renderers with templates and typing plus JSON serialization.

---

## Quick start

A simple CLI with a `hello` command:

```rust
use tap::{
    argsparsing::ArgsP,
    engine::structs::{CmdInfo, Engine, ErrorType},
    tooling::console::engine::add_help_handler,
};

fn hello_handler(_: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    let name = args.first().unwrap_or(&"World");
    println!("Hello, {}!", name);
    Ok(())
}

fn main() {
    let mut ap = ArgsP::new();
    let mut engine = Engine::new(&mut ap, "MyApp v1.0".to_string());

    engine.new_command(
        "hello",
        CmdInfo::new(hello_handler, vec![], vec!["name"], false, "Say hello"),
    );

    add_help_handler(vec!["help", "-h"], &mut engine);

    if let Err(e) = engine.main() {
        eprintln!("Error: {}", e);
    }
}
```

Run:

```bash
$ cargo run hello Rust
Hello, Rust!
$ cargo run hello
Hello, World!
$ cargo run help
MyApp v1.0

╭───────  Command [help OR -h]
⎬─ Args: (none)
⎬─ Docs:
│     Generate and print help message
╰─────── 
╭───────  Command [hello]
⎬─ Args: [name]
⎬─ Docs:
│     Say hello
╰─────── 
```

The box-drawing characters in the `help` output are what `generate_help` actually prints. Not a README decoration.

---

## Commands and arguments

```rust
fn my_handler(e: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType { ... }

engine.new_command(
    "copy",                               // command name
    CmdInfo::new(
        my_handler,                       // handler function
        vec!["src", "dst"],               // required arguments
        vec!["force"],                    // optional
        false,                            // unlimited: if true, accepts any number of extra arguments
        "Copy source to destination",     // description for help
    ),
);
```

The help will show:

```
╭───────  Command [copy]
⎬─ Args: <src>, <dst>, [force]
⎬─ Docs:
│     Copy source to destination
╰─────── 
```

---

## Flags

Flags are written as `--flag`, `--key=value`, `--key:value`. They are parsed automatically in `ArgsP`:

- `args_p.flags` - list of flags without values.
- `args_p.values` - dictionary key -> value.

Reading in a handler:

```rust
fn my_handler(e: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    if e.args_p.flags.contains(&"verbose".to_string()) {
        println!("Verbose mode enabled");
    }
    if let Some(out) = e.args_p.values.get("output") {
        println!("Output file: {}", out);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Important: flags are stripped from `args` before the handler is called. Access them only via `e.args_p`.

---

## Colors

Colored output via `[?COLOR]` codes:

- `[?GN]`, `[?GREEN]` - green
- `[?BGN]`, `[?BGREEN]` - bright green
- `[?BACKGREEN]`, `[?BKGN]` - green background
- `[?BACKBGREEN]`, `[?BKBGN]` - bright green background
- `[?BOLD]`, `[?BD]` - bold
- `[?DIM]`, `[?DM]` - dim
- `[?ITALIC]`, `[?IT]` - italic
- `[?UNDERLINE]`, `[?UE]` - underline
- `[?BLINK]`, `[?BL]` - blinking
- `[?REVERSE]`, `[?RV]` - reverse
- `[?STRIKETHROUGH]`, `[?ST]` - strikethrough
- `[?RT]` - reset

Format: `[?<BACKGROUND><BRIGHT><COLOR>]`.

- `<BACKGROUND>` - prefix `BK` (short) or `BACK` (full) for background.
- `<BRIGHT>` - prefix `B` for the bright variant.
- `<COLOR>` - name or two letters (first and last letter of the name). Example: `GN` = green.

### Palette

**Standard 16**: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, and their bright variants. All are available as background.

**Extended (xterm-256)**: also available as background:

| Name      | Abbr. | Name        | Abbr. |
|-----------|-------|-------------|-------|
| orange    | `OE`  | lime        | `LE`  |
| pink      | `PK`  | teal        | `TL`  |
| purple    | `PE`  | navy        | `NY`  |
| violet    | `VT`  | gold        | `GD`  |
| brown     | `BN`  | silver      | `SR`  |
| gray      | `GY`  | maroon      | `MN`  |

Examples: `[?OE]` - orange, `[?BACKGOLD]` / `[?BKGD]` - gold background, `[?BKOE]` - orange background.

### Styles

`BOLD` (`BD`), `DIM`/`FAINT` (`DM`), `ITALIC` (`IT`), `UNDERLINE` (`UE`), `BLINK` (`BL`), `REVERSE` (`RV`), `STRIKETHROUGH` (`ST`), `RESET` (`RT`).

### Usage

```rust
use tap::tooling::colors::print::println;
use tap::tooling::colors::set::colorize;

let raw = "[?GN]Success![?RT] File saved as [?YW]config.toml[?RT]";

println(raw);                       // prints already colored
let colored: String = colorize(raw); // or get a string
```

`println`/`print` in `colors::print` already call `colorize` internally - no need to colorize twice.

Disable colors globally:

```rust
use tap::tooling::colors::set::COLOR_ENABLED;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

COLOR_ENABLED.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
```

Unknown codes (`[?FOO]`) are not consumed or turned into garbage - they remain in the string as-is. This is convenient for debugging.

---

## Grouping commands in help

Commands with identical `CmdInfo` are automatically grouped into one line as aliases:

```rust
engine.new_commands(
    vec!["help", "-h"],
    CmdInfo::new(help_handler, vec![], vec![], false, "Show help"),
);
```

The help will show `[help / -h]`.

`required`, `optional`, `unlimited`, and `docs` are compared. If `docs` differ, there will be no grouping.

---

## Renderers

The `tooling::renderable` module allows templating output by scope:

```rust
use tap::tooling::renderable::{
    Renderable, add_template_render, add_template_render_colored,
};

let mut r = Renderable::new();
r.scope.insert("name", "Rust");
r.scope.insert("version:int", "1");     // :int - validated as a number
r.scope.insert("stable:bool", "true");  // :bool - only "true"/"false"

add_template_render("Hello, {{name}} (v{{version}})", "plain", &mut r);
add_template_render_colored("[?GN]Hello, {{name}}[?RT]", "colored", &mut r);

println!("{}", r.render_with("plain").unwrap());
println!("{}", r.render_with("colored").unwrap());
println!("{}", r.render_json().unwrap()); // {"name":"Rust","stable":true,"version":1}
```

`render_json` returns a `Result` - for an invalid `:int`/`:bool` it returns `RenderError::InvalidValue` rather than silently inserting garbage into JSON.

---

> MIT - see the LICENSE file for details.
> 2026, By Pt.
````

## `src/tap/argsparsing.rs`

```rust
use std::{collections::HashMap, str::FromStr};

pub struct ArgsP {
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    pub flags: Vec<String>,
    pub values: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl ArgsP {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            args: vec![],
            flags: vec![],
            values: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    fn count_leading_same_chars(s: &str) -> usize {
        let mut chars = s.chars();
        match chars.next() {
            Some(first) => 1 + chars.take_while(|&c| c == first).count(),
            None => 0,
        }
    }

    fn parse_args(args: &[&str]) -> (Vec<String>, HashMap<String, String>, Vec<String>) {
        let mut flags: Vec<String> = vec![];
        let mut values: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
        let mut r_args: Vec<String> = vec![];
        let mut can_be_flag = true;
        for arg in args {
            let mut split: Vec<&str> = arg.splitn(2, "=").collect();
            if split.len() == 1 {
                split = arg.splitn(2, ":").collect();
            }
            let s0 = split[0];
            let sch = Self::count_leading_same_chars(s0);

            if *arg == "--" && can_be_flag {
                can_be_flag = !can_be_flag;
                continue;
            }

            if s0.starts_with("--") && s0.len() > sch && sch < 3 && can_be_flag {
                if split.len() > 1 {
                    values.insert(s0[sch..].to_string(), split[1].to_string());
                } else {
                    flags.push(s0[sch..].to_string());
                }
            } else {
                r_args.push(arg.to_string());
            }
        }
        (flags, values, r_args)
    }

    pub fn parse_args_to_self(&mut self, args: &[&str]) {
        let (flags, values, r_args) = Self::parse_args(args);
        self.flags = flags;
        self.values = values;
        self.args = r_args;
    }
}


pub trait ArgsExt {
    fn arg<T: FromStr>(&self, i: usize) -> Result<T, String>
    where
        T::Err: std::fmt::Display;

    fn arg_or<'a>(&'a self, i: usize, default: &'a str) -> &'a str;
}

impl ArgsExt for [&str] {
    fn arg<T: FromStr>(&self, i: usize) -> Result<T, String>
    where
        T::Err: std::fmt::Display,
    {
        self.get(i)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("missing argument #{}", i))?
            .parse()
            .map_err(|e| format!("invalid argument #{}: {}", i, e))
    }

    fn arg_or<'a>(&'a self, i: usize, default: &'a str) -> &'a str {
        self.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(default)
    }
}
```

````rust
//! Convenience macros and helper functions for `tap`.
//!
//! # Enabling
//!
//! This module is not wired up automatically. Add it in `src/tap/mod.rs`:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! pub mod macros;
//! ```
//!
//! All macros are exported at the crate root (`#[macro_export]`), so call them
//! through the crate name — e.g. `tap::commands! { ... }`, `tap::bail!(...)`,
//! `tap::cprintln!(...)`.
//!
//! # Contents
//!
//! | Category             | Items                                                                    |
//! |----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
//! | Helpers              | [`arg`], [`arg_str`], [`arg_or`], [`arg_str_or`], [`arg_str_opt`]        |
//! | Registration         | [`commands!`], [`subcommands!`]                                          |
//! | Argument parsing     | [`args!`]                                                                |
//! | Errors               | [`bail!`], [`ensure!`]                                                   |
//! | Output               | [`cprint!`], [`cprintln!`], [`ceprintln!`]                               |
//! | Scopes / templates   | [`scope!`], [`template!`], [`template_colored!`]                         |
//!
//! # Typical usage
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use tap::{commands, args, bail, ensure};
//!
//! commands! {
//!     engine;
//!     "add" | "a" => my_add {
//!         required: ["x", "y"],
//!         docs: "Add two numbers",
//!     }
//!     "greet" => my_greet {
//!         required: ["name"],
//!         optional: ["greeting"],
//!         docs: "Say hello",
//!     }
//! }
//!
//! fn my_add(_: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
//!     args! { args;
//!         x: i64,
//!         y: i64,
//!     }
//!     println!("{}", x + y);
//!     Ok(())
//! }
//! ```

use std::str::FromStr;

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  Helper functions
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Parses a required argument at index `i` into type `T`.
///
/// Returns an error when:
///
/// * no argument exists at index `i` — `"missing argument <name> (position i)"`;
/// * the argument exists but fails to parse as `T` — `"argument <name>: <parser error>"`.
///
/// The error message includes `name` so users can tell which argument was
/// wrong rather than receiving a bare parser error.
pub fn arg<'a, T>(args: &[&'a str], i: usize, name: &str) -> Result<T, String>
where
    T: FromStr,
    T::Err: std::fmt::Display,
{
    let s = args
        .get(i)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("missing argument <{}> (position {})", name, i))?;
    s.parse()
        .map_err(|e| format!("argument <{}>: {}", name, e))
}

/// Returns a required argument at index `i` as a string slice.
///
/// Unlike [`arg`], no parsing is performed. Errors only when the argument is
/// missing.
pub fn arg_str<'a>(args: &[&'a str], i: usize, name: &str) -> Result<&'a str, String> {
    args.get(i)
        .copied()
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("missing argument <{}> (position {})", name, i))
}

/// Like [`arg`], but falls back to `default` when the argument is absent.
///
/// Parsing errors are still reported — if the argument is present, it must
/// parse as `T`.
pub fn arg_or<'a, T>(args: &[&'a str], i: usize, name: &str, default: T) -> Result<T, String>
where
    T: FromStr,
    T::Err: std::fmt::Display,
{
    match args.get(i) {
        Some(s) => s.parse().map_err(|e| format!("argument <{}>: {}", name, e)),
        None => Ok(default),
    }
}

/// Like [`arg_str`], but returns `default` when the argument is absent.
///
/// Never fails.
pub fn arg_str_or<'a>(args: &[&'a str], i: usize, default: &'a str) -> &'a str {
    args.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(default)
}

/// Returns the argument at index `i` if present, otherwise `None`.
///
/// Never fails.
pub fn arg_str_opt<'a>(args: &[&'a str], i: usize) -> Option<&'a str> {
    args.get(i).copied()
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  commands!
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Registers one or more top-level commands on an engine.
///
/// Each entry has the shape:
///
/// ```ignore
/// "name" | "alias" => handler {
///     required: ["arg1", "arg2"],   // optional field
///     optional: ["arg3"],           // optional field
///     unlimited: true,              // optional, defaults to false
///     docs: "Description",          // required
/// }
/// ```
///
/// All fields except `docs` may be omitted. `required`, `optional` and
/// `unlimited` default to empty/false.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```ignore
/// tap::commands! {
///     engine;
///     "echo" => cmd_echo {
///         required: ["text"],
///         docs: "Echo back the text",
///     }
///     "quit" | "exit" => cmd_quit {
///         docs: "Exit the shell",
///     }
/// }
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! commands {
    (
        $engine:ident;
        $(
            $($name:literal)|+ => $handler:path {
                $(required: [$($req:literal),* $(,)?],)?
                $(optional: [$($opt:literal),* $(,)?],)?
                $(unlimited: $unlim:literal,)?
                docs: $docs:literal $(,)?
            }
        )*
    ) => {{
        $(
            $engine.new_commands(
                vec![$($name),+],
                {
                    let __tap_h: $crate::engine::structs::HandlerType =
                        ::std::rc::Rc::new($handler);
                    $crate::engine::structs::CmdInfo::new(
                        __tap_h,
                        vec![$($($req),*)?],
                        vec![$($($opt),*)?],
                        $crate::commands!(@unlim $($unlim)?),
                        $docs,
                    )
                },
            );
        )*
    }};

    (@unlim $b:literal) => { $b };
    (@unlim)            => { false };
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  subcommands!
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Registers one or more subcommands on an engine.
///
/// Syntax is identical to [`commands!`], except that the handler must be a
/// `SubHandlerType` (a plain function pointer, not an `Rc`).
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```ignore
/// tap::subcommands! {
///     engine;
///     "set" => sub_set {
///         required: ["key", "value"],
///         docs: "Set a variable",
///     }
/// }
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! subcommands {
    (
        $engine:ident;
        $(
            $($name:literal)|+ => $handler:path {
                $(required: [$($req:literal),* $(,)?],)?
                $(optional: [$($opt:literal),* $(,)?],)?
                $(unlimited: $unlim:literal,)?
                docs: $docs:literal $(,)?
            }
        )*
    ) => {{
        $(
            $engine.new_subcommands(
                vec![$($name),+],
                $crate::engine::structs::CmdInfo::new(
                    $handler as $crate::engine::structs::SubHandlerType,
                    vec![$($($req),*)?],
                    vec![$($($opt),*)?],
                    $crate::subcommands!(@unlim $($unlim)?),
                    $docs,
                ),
            );
        )*
    }};

    (@unlim $b:literal) => { $b };
    (@unlim)            => { false };
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  args!
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Binds handler arguments to typed local variables.
///
/// Syntax: `args! { <slice>; name: Type, name: Type = default, ... }`.
///
/// * `name: Type`             — required, parsed via [`arg`].
/// * `name: Type = default`   — optional, parsed via [`arg_or`].
///
/// Each variable consumes one positional argument, so the order matters.
/// The trailing comma is allowed and optional.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```ignore
/// fn handler(_: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
///     args! { args;
///         count: u32,
///         label: String = "default".to_string(),
///         verbose: bool = false,
///     }
///     // ...
///     Ok(())
/// }
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! args {
    ($args:expr; $($rest:tt)*) => {
        let __tap_args: &[&str] = $args;
        let mut __tap_i: usize = 0usize;
        $crate::args!(@next __tap_args, __tap_i, $($rest)*);
        let _ = __tap_i;
    };

    (@next $args:ident, $i:ident,) => {};

    (@next $args:ident, $i:ident, $name:ident : $ty:ty = $default:expr, $($rest:tt)*) => {
        let $name: $ty = $crate::macros::arg_or(
            $args, $i, stringify!($name), $default
        )?;
        $i += 1;
        $crate::args!(@next $args, $i, $($rest)*);
    };

    (@next $args:ident, $i:ident, $name:ident : $ty:ty = $default:expr) => {
        let $name: $ty = $crate::macros::arg_or(
            $args, $i, stringify!($name), $default
        )?;
        $i += 1;
        $crate::args!(@next $args, $i,);
    };

    (@next $args:ident, $i:ident, $name:ident : $ty:ty, $($rest:tt)*) => {
        let $name: $ty = $crate::macros::arg(
            $args, $i, stringify!($name)
        )?;
        $i += 1;
        $crate::args!(@next $args, $i, $($rest)*);
    };

    (@next $args:ident, $i:ident, $name:ident : $ty:ty) => {
        let $name: $ty = $crate::macros::arg(
            $args, $i, stringify!($name)
        )?;
        $i += 1;
        $crate::args!(@next $args, $i,);
    };
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  Error helpers — `bail!` / `ensure!`
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Early-returns an error from a handler.
///
/// Accepts either a literal/expression convertible into the handler's error
/// type, or a `format!`-style format string with arguments.
///
/// ```ignore
/// fn h(_: &mut Engine, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
///     if args.is_empty() { bail!("at least one argument required"); }
///     let n: u32 = args[0].parse().map_err(|_| format!("bad number: {}", args[0]))?;
///     ensure!(n > 0, "must be positive, got {}", n);
///     Ok(())
/// }
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! bail {
    ($msg:literal $(,)?) => {
        return ::std::result::Result::Err($msg.into())
    };
    ($err:expr $(,)?) => {
        return ::std::result::Result::Err($err.into())
    };
    ($fmt:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => {
        return ::std::result::Result::Err(format!($fmt, $($arg)*).into())
    };
}

/// Conditional [`bail!`]: returns an error when the condition is false.
///
/// ```ignore
/// ensure!(count <= 10, "too many items: {}", count);
/// ensure!(flag, "flag must be set");
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ensure {
    ($cond:expr, $msg:literal $(,)?) => {
        if !$cond { $crate::bail!($msg) }
    };
    ($cond:expr, $err:expr $(,)?) => {
        if !$cond { $crate::bail!($err) }
    };
    ($cond:expr, $fmt:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => {
        if !$cond { $crate::bail!($fmt, $($arg)*) }
    };
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  Colored printing — `cprint!` / `cprintln!` / `ceprintln!`
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Colored `print!`.
///
/// The formatted string is passed through
/// `tooling::colors::set::colorize` before writing to stdout.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! cprint {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {
        ::std::print!("{}", $crate::tooling::colors::set::colorize(&format!($($arg)*)))
    };
}

/// Colored `println!`.
///
/// With no arguments, emits a plain newline (no colorization needed).
/// Otherwise formats and colorizes the output.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! cprintln {
    () => { ::std::println!() };
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {
        ::std::println!("{}", $crate::tooling::colors::set::colorize(&format!($($arg)*)))
    };
}

/// Colored `eprintln!` — writes to stderr.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ceprintln {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {
        ::std::eprintln!("{}", $crate::tooling::colors::set::colorize(&format!($($arg)*)))
    };
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  Renderable shortcuts — `scope!` / `template!` / `template_colored!`
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Populates `Renderable::scope` with `key => value` pairs.
///
/// The `key` may include a `:type` suffix (e.g. `"version:int"`) that is
/// interpreted by the renderer downstream.
///
/// ```ignore
/// scope!(r;
///     "name" => "Rust",
///     "version:int" => "1",
///     "stable:bool" => "true",
/// );
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! scope {
    ($r:expr; $($key:literal => $val:expr),* $(,)?) => {{
        $($r.scope.insert($key, $val);)*
    }};
}

/// Adds a plain template renderer.
///
/// ```ignore
/// template!(r, "plain", "Hello, {{name}}");
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! template {
    ($r:expr, $name:expr, $templ:expr) => {
        $crate::tooling::renderable::add_template_render($templ, $name, &mut $r)
    };
}

/// Adds a colored template renderer.
///
/// The rendered result is passed through `colorize`, so `[?GN]…[?RT]` style
/// color codes are resolved.
///
/// ```ignore
/// template_colored!(r, "colored", "[?GN]Hello, {{name}}[?RT]");
/// ```
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! template_colored {
    ($r:expr, $name:expr, $templ:expr) => {
        $crate::tooling::renderable::add_template_render_colored($templ, $name, &mut $r)
    };
}
````

## `src/tap/tooling/renderable.rs`

```rust
use std::{collections::HashMap, error::Error, fmt, sync::Arc};

use string_template::Template;

use crate::tooling::colors::set::colorize;

type RenderScopeT<'a> = HashMap<&'a str, &'a str>;
type RendererT<'a> = Arc<dyn Fn(&RenderScopeT<'a>) -> Result<String, Box<dyn Error>> + 'a>;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum RenderError {
    RendererNotFound(String),
    RendererError(Box<dyn Error>),
    InvalidValue {
        key: String,
        kind: &'static str,
        value: String,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for RenderError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::RendererNotFound(name) => write!(f, "renderer not found: {name}"),
            Self::RendererError(err) => write!(f, "renderer error: {err}"),
            Self::InvalidValue { key, kind, value } => {
                write!(f, "{key:?}:{kind} has invalid value: {value:?}")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Error for RenderError {}

#[derive(Default, Clone)]
pub struct Renderable<'a> {
    pub renderers: HashMap<String, RendererT<'a>>,
    pub scope: RenderScopeT<'a>,
}

impl<'a> fmt::Debug for Renderable<'a> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("Renderable")
            .field("renderers", &self.renderers.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>())
            .field("scope", &self.scope)
            .finish()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Kind {
    Str,
    Int,
    Float,
    Bool,
    Raw,
}

fn split_kind(key: &str) -> (&str, Kind) {
    if let Some(k) = key.strip_suffix(":int") {
        (k, Kind::Int)
    } else if let Some(k) = key.strip_suffix(":float") {
        (k, Kind::Float)
    } else if let Some(k) = key.strip_suffix(":bool") {
        (k, Kind::Bool)
    } else if let Some(k) = key.strip_suffix(":raw") {
        (k, Kind::Raw)
    } else {
        (key, Kind::Str)
    }
}

impl<'a> Renderable<'a> {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn render_json(&self) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
        let mut items: Vec<(&str, &str, Kind)> = self
            .scope
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| {
                let (name, kind) = split_kind(k);
                (name, *v, kind)
            })
            .collect();
        items.sort_by_key(|(name, _, _)| *name);

        let mut out = String::from("{");
        for (i, (name, value, kind)) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                out.push(',');
            }
            push_json_string(&mut out, name);
            out.push(':');
            match kind {
                Kind::Str => push_json_string(&mut out, value),
                Kind::Int => {
                    if !is_json_int(value) {
                        return Err(RenderError::InvalidValue {
                            key: name.to_string(),
                            kind: "int",
                            value: value.to_string(),
                        });
                    }
                    out.push_str(value);
                }
                Kind::Float => {
                    if !is_json_number(value) {
                        return Err(RenderError::InvalidValue {
                            key: name.to_string(),
                            kind: "float",
                            value: value.to_string(),
                        });
                    }
                    out.push_str(value);
                }
                Kind::Bool => {
                    if value != "true" && value != "false" {
                        return Err(RenderError::InvalidValue {
                            key: name.to_string(),
                            kind: "bool",
                            value: value.to_string(),
                        });
                    }
                    out.push_str(value);
                }
                Kind::Raw => out.push_str(value),
            }
        }
        out.push('}');
        Ok(out)
    }

    pub fn render_with(&self, name: &str) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
        let renderer = self
            .renderers
            .get(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| RenderError::RendererNotFound(name.to_string()))?;

        let mut scope: RenderScopeT<'a> = HashMap::with_capacity(self.scope.len());
        for (k, v) in &self.scope {
            let (key, _) = split_kind(k);
            scope.insert(key, v);
        }

        renderer(&scope).map_err(RenderError::RendererError)
    }
}

pub fn render_json_array(rows: &[Renderable<'_>]) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
    let parts: Vec<String> = rows
        .iter()
        .map(Renderable::render_json)
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    Ok(format!("[{}]", parts.join(",")))
}

pub fn add_template_render<'a>(
    templ: &'a str,
    name: impl Into<String>,
    renderable: &mut Renderable<'a>,
) {
    let template = Template::new(templ);
    let func: RendererT<'a> = Arc::new(
        move |scope: &RenderScopeT<'a>| -> Result<String, Box<dyn Error>> {
            Ok(template.render(scope))
        },
    );
    renderable.renderers.insert(name.into(), func);
}

pub fn add_template_render_colored<'a>(
    templ: &'a str,
    name: impl Into<String>,
    renderable: &mut Renderable<'a>,
) {
    let template = Template::new(templ);
    let func: RendererT<'a> = Arc::new(
        move |scope: &RenderScopeT<'a>| -> Result<String, Box<dyn Error>> {
            Ok(colorize(&template.render(scope)))
        },
    );
    renderable.renderers.insert(name.into(), func);
}

fn push_json_string(out: &mut String, s: &str) {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    out.push('"');
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            '\u{08}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\u{0C}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {
                let _ = write!(out, "\\u{:04x}", c as u32);
            }
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
}

// JSON int: -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)
fn is_json_int(s: &str) -> bool {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut i = 0;
    if i < b.len() && b[i] == b'-' {
        i += 1;
    }
    match b.get(i) {
        Some(b'0') => i += 1,
        Some(c) if c.is_ascii_digit() => {
            while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
                i += 1;
            }
        }
        _ => return false,
    }
    i == b.len()
}

// JSON number: -?int(\.\d+)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?
fn is_json_number(s: &str) -> bool {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut i = 0;
    if i < b.len() && b[i] == b'-' {
        i += 1;
    }
    match b.get(i) {
        Some(b'0') => i += 1,
        Some(c) if c.is_ascii_digit() => {
            while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
                i += 1;
            }
        }
        _ => return false,
    }
    if i < b.len() && b[i] == b'.' {
        i += 1;
        if i >= b.len() || !b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
            return false;
        }
        while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'e' || b[i] == b'E') {
        i += 1;
        if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'+' || b[i] == b'-') {
            i += 1;
        }
        if i >= b.len() || !b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
            return false;
        }
        while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    i == b.len()
}
```

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

use crate::tooling::console::{colors, styles::Text};

pub static COLOR_ENABLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(true);

pub fn colorize(s: &str) -> String {
    let colored = COLOR_ENABLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    let mut text = Text::new();
    colors::colorize(s, &mut text);
    text.get(colored)
}
```

use crate::{
    engine::structs::{CmdInfo, Engine},
    tooling::{
        colors::set::colorize,
        formatting::text::{add_space, frame},
    },
};

#[derive(PartialEq)]
pub struct HelpCmdInfo<'a, H> {
    pub commands: Vec<String>,
    pub info: &'a CmdInfo<'a, H>,
}

impl<'a, H> HelpCmdInfo<'a, H> {
    pub fn new(command: String, info: &'a CmdInfo<'a, H>) -> Self {
        Self {
            commands: vec![command],
            info: info,
        }
    }

    pub fn is(&mut self, name: String, info: &CmdInfo<'a, H>) -> bool {
        let same = self.info.required == info.required
            && self.info.optional == info.optional
            && self.info.unlimited == info.unlimited
            && self.info.docs == info.docs;
        if same {
            self.commands.push(name);
        }
        same
    }
}

pub fn group_commands<'a, C, H>(commands: &'a C) -> Vec<HelpCmdInfo<'a, H>>
where
    &'a C: IntoIterator<Item = (&'a &'a str, &'a CmdInfo<'a, H>)>,
{
    let mut grouped: Vec<HelpCmdInfo<H>> = Vec::new();
    for (name, info) in commands {
        let mut added = false;
        for cmd in &mut grouped {
            if cmd.is(name.to_string(), info) {
                added = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if !added {
            grouped.push(HelpCmdInfo::new(name.to_string(), info));
        }
    }
    grouped
}

pub fn generate_help(eng: &Engine) -> String {
    let mut res = String::from("");
    // === Paste about ===
    if eng.about.trim() != "" {
        res.push_str(&format!("{}", colorize(&eng.about)));
        res.push_str("\n\n");
    }
    // === Paste basic handler docs after about ===
    match eng.basic_handler {
        Some(ref i) => {
            let docs = i.docs;
            if docs.trim() != "" {
                res.push_str(docs);
                res.push_str("\n\n");
            }
        }
        None => {}
    }
    // === Generating commands help ===
    let mut cmds_keys: Vec<&str> = eng.cmds.keys().copied().collect();
    cmds_keys.sort_unstable();
    let mut commands: Vec<HelpCmdInfo<'_, _>> = Vec::new();
    for name in cmds_keys.iter().copied() {
        let info = eng.cmds.get(name).unwrap();
        let mut added = false;
        for cmd in &mut commands {
            if cmd.is(name.to_string(), info) {
                added = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if !added {
            commands.push(HelpCmdInfo::new(name.to_string(), info));
        }
    }
    for cmd in commands {
        let mut argsv: Vec<String> = vec![];
        for req in &cmd.info.required {
            let r = format!("[?RD]<{}>[?RT]", req.to_string());
            argsv.push(r);
        }
        for opt in &cmd.info.optional {
            let r = format!("[?BE][{}][?RT]", opt.to_string());
            argsv.push(r);
        }
        if cmd.info.unlimited {
            argsv.push("[?CN](arg...)[?RT]".to_string());
        }
        if argsv.len() == 0 {
            argsv.push("(none)".to_string());
        }
        let args = colorize(&argsv.join(", "));
        let block = &format!(
            "- [?YW]Args[?RT]: {}\n- [?YW]Docs[?RT]:\n{}",
            args,
            add_space(&cmd.info.docs, " ", 1)
        );
        let cmd = &colorize(&format!(
            "[?BGN] Command [?BKBK][?BBK][[?BKBK][?YW]{}[?BBK]][?RT]",
            cmd.commands.join(" [?GN]OR[?YW] ")
        ));
        res.push_str(&frame(block, cmd, "", "GN"));
        res.push('\n');
    }
    // === Generating subcommands help ===
    let mut subcmds_keys: Vec<&str> = eng.subcmds.keys().copied().collect();
    subcmds_keys.sort_unstable();
    let mut subcommands: Vec<HelpCmdInfo<'_, _>> = Vec::new();
    for name in subcmds_keys.iter().copied() {
        let info = eng.subcmds.get(name).unwrap();
        let mut added = false;
        for cmd in &mut subcommands {
            if cmd.is(name.to_string(), info) {
                added = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if !added {
            subcommands.push(HelpCmdInfo::new(name.to_string(), info));
        }
    }
    for cmd in subcommands {
        let block = &format!("- [?YW]Docs[?RT]:\n{}", add_space(&cmd.info.docs, " ", 1));
        let cmd = &colorize(&format!(
            "[?BGN] Command [?BKBK][?BBK][[?BKBK][?YW]{}[?BBK]][?RT]",
            cmd.commands.join(" [?GN]OR[?YW] ")
        ));
        res.push_str(&frame(block, cmd, "", "GN"));
        res.push('\n');
    }
    res
}

use crate::tooling::colors::set::colorize;

pub fn frame(text: &str, prefix: &str, postfix: &str, color: &str) -> String {
    let mut res = vec![format!("[?{}]╭─────── [?RT]{}", color, prefix)];
    for line in text.split("\n") {
        if line.starts_with("-") {
            res.push(format!("[?{}]⎬─[?RT]{}", color, line.replacen("-", "", 1)));
        } else {
            res.push(format!("[?{}]│    [?RT]{}", color, line));
        }
    }
    res.push(format!("[?{}]╰─────── [?RT]{}", color, postfix));
    colorize(res.join("\n").as_str())
}

pub fn add_space(text: &str, space: &str, n_spaces: usize) -> String {
    let space = &space.repeat(n_spaces);
    let mut res = String::from(space);
    res.push_str(&text.replace("\n", space));
    res
}

pub fn colorize(inp: &str, text: &mut Text) {
    let table = colors();
    let mut rest = inp;
    while !rest.is_empty() {
        if let Some(after) = rest.strip_prefix("[?") {
            let close = after
                .char_indices()
                .find(|(i, c)| *c == ']' && *i < 32)
                .map(|(i, _)| i);
            if let Some(close) = close {
                let code = &after[..close];
                if let Some(col) = table.get(code) {
                    let mut s = Str::new();
                    s.colors.add(*col);
                    text.text.push(s);
                    rest = &after[close + 1..];
                    continue;
                }
            }
        }
        let ch = rest.chars().next().unwrap();
        let l = text.text.len();
        if l > 0 {
            text.text[l - 1].text.push(ch);
        } else {
            let mut s = Str::new();
            s.text.push(ch);
            text.text.push(s);
        }
        rest = &rest[ch.len_utf8()..];
    }
}

```rust
use crate::tooling::console::{
    colors::colorize,
    styles::{Str, Text},
};

pub struct Console {
    pub buf: Vec<Text>,
    pub colored: bool,
}

impl Console {
    pub fn new(colored: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            buf: vec![],
            colored: colored,
        }
    }

    pub fn addc(&mut self, text: &str, new: bool) -> &mut Self {
        let mut toappend = Text::new();
        colorize(text, &mut toappend);
        self.addraw(&mut toappend, new)
    }

    pub fn add(&mut self, text: &str, new: bool) -> &mut Self {
        let mut toappend = Text::new();
        toappend.text.push(Str::new().add(text).clone());
        self.addraw(&mut toappend, new)
    }

    fn addraw(&mut self, text: &mut Text, new: bool) -> &mut Self {
        if new || self.buf.is_empty() {
            self.buf.push(text.clone());
        } else {
            let last = self.buf.last_mut().unwrap();
            last.text.append(&mut text.text);
        }
        self
    }

    pub fn clear(&mut self) -> &mut Self {
        self.buf = vec![];
        self
    }

    pub fn get(&self, colored: bool) -> String {
        let mut lines: Vec<String> = vec![];
        for line in self.buf.iter() {
            lines.push(line.get(colored));
        }
        lines.join("\n")
    }

    pub fn print(&self) {
        print!("{}", self.get(self.colored));
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Color {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub code: &'static str,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Colors {
    codes: Vec<Color>,
}

impl Colors {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { codes: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn add(&mut self, c: Color) -> &mut Self {
        self.codes.push(c);
        self
    }

    pub fn rem(&mut self, name: &str) -> &mut Self {
        self.codes.retain(|c| c.name != name);
        self
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> String {
        let mut res = String::new();
        for col in &self.codes {
            res.push_str(col.code);
        }
        res
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.codes.is_empty()
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Str {
    pub text: String,
    pub colors: Colors,
}

impl Str {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            text: "".to_string(),
            colors: Colors::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn add(&mut self, text: &str) -> &mut Self {
        self.text += text;
        self
    }

    pub fn get(&self, colored: bool) -> String {
        let mut res = String::from("");
        if colored {
            res += self.colors.get().as_str();
        }
        res += self.text.as_str();
        res
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Text {
    pub text: Vec<Str>,
}

impl Text {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { text: vec![] }
    }

    pub fn get(&self, colored: bool) -> String {
        let mut res = String::from("");
        for text in self.text.iter() {
            res.push_str(&text.get(colored));
        }
        res
    }
}

## `src/tap/engine/dispatching.rs`

```rust
use std::rc::Rc;

use crate::engine::structs::{CmdInfo, Engine, ErrorType};

fn validate_args<H>(info: &CmdInfo<'_, H>, args: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    let ln = args.len();
    let r = &info.required;
    let o = &info.optional;
    let u = info.unlimited;
    if ln < r.len() {
        return Some(format!(
            "Missing arguments: expected at least {}, got {} ({})",
            r.len(),
            ln,
            r.join(", ")
        ));
    }
    if ln > r.len() + o.len() && !u {
        return Some(format!(
            "Too many arguments: expected at most {}, got {}",
            r.len() + o.len(),
            ln
        ));
    }
    None
}

impl Engine<'_> {
    pub fn process(&mut self, cmd: &str, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
        let err: ErrorType;
        if let Some(info) = self.cmds.get(cmd) {
            if let Some(err) = validate_args(info, args) {
                return Err(err.into());
            }
            let handler = Rc::clone(&info.handler);
            err = handler(self, args);
        } else if let Some(info) = self.subcmds.get(cmd) {
            if let Some(err) = validate_args(info, args) {
                return Err(err.into());
            }
            err = (info.handler)(args);
        } else if let Some(info) = &self.basic_handler {
            let mut _args = vec![cmd];
            _args.extend(args);
            if let Some(err) = validate_args(info, &_args) {
                return Err(err.into());
            }
            let handler = Rc::clone(&info.handler);
            err = handler(self, &_args);
        } else {
            err = Err("Invalid command: not found".into());
        }
        match err {
            Err(e) => return Err(format!("Process Error: {}", e).into()),
            Ok(_) => return Ok(()),
        }
    }
}

use crate::argsparsing::ArgsP;
use crate::engine::structs::{
    BasicHandler, CmdInfoCmd, CmdInfoSubcmd, CmdMap, Engine, ErrorType, SubCmdsMap,
};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::str::FromStr;

pub struct EngineGetter<'a> {
    pub e: &'a Engine<'a>,
}

impl<'a> EngineGetter<'a> {
    pub fn new(e: &'a Engine<'a>) -> Self {
        Self { e: e }
    }

    pub fn get_cmds(&self) -> &CmdMap<'a> {
        return &self.e.cmds;
    }

    pub fn get_subcmds(&self) -> &SubCmdsMap<'a> {
        return &self.e.subcmds;
    }

    pub fn basic_handler(&self) -> &BasicHandler<'a> {
        return &self.e.basic_handler;
    }
}

impl<'a> Engine<'a> {
    pub fn new(args_p: &'a mut ArgsP, about: String) -> Self {
        Self {
            args_p,
            cmds: HashMap::new(),
            subcmds: HashMap::new(),
            basic_handler: None,
            about: about,
        }
    }

    pub fn getter(&'a self) -> EngineGetter<'a> {
        return EngineGetter::new(self);
    }

    pub fn new_command(&mut self, name: &'a str, cmdinfo: CmdInfoCmd<'a>) {
        self.cmds.insert(name, cmdinfo);
    }

    pub fn new_commands(&mut self, names: Vec<&'a str>, cmdinfo: CmdInfoCmd<'a>) {
        for name in names {
            self.new_command(name, cmdinfo.clone());
        }
    }

    pub fn new_subcommand(&mut self, name: &'a str, cmdinfo: CmdInfoSubcmd<'a>) {
        self.subcmds.insert(name, cmdinfo);
    }

    pub fn new_subcommands(&mut self, names: Vec<&'a str>, cmdinfo: CmdInfoSubcmd<'a>) {
        for name in names {
            self.new_subcommand(name, cmdinfo.clone());
        }
    }

    pub fn work(&mut self, args: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
        self.args_p.parse_args_to_self(args);
        if self.args_p.args.is_empty() {
            println!("{}", self.about);
            return Err("No command provided".into());
        }
        let all_args = self.args_p.args.clone();
        let cmd = all_args[0].as_str();
        let args_refs: Vec<&str> = all_args[1..].iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
        self.process(cmd, &args_refs)
    }

    pub fn main(&mut self) -> ErrorType {
        let args: Vec<String> = env::args().skip(1).collect();
        let refs: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
        self.work(&refs)
    }
}

impl Engine<'_> {
    pub fn flag(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.args_p.flags.iter().any(|f| f == name)
    }

    pub fn value(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.args_p.values.get(name).map(String::as_str)
    }

    pub fn value_t<T: FromStr>(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<T>, String>
    where
        T::Err: std::fmt::Display,
    {
        match self.args_p.values.get(name) {
            Some(s) => s.parse().map(Some).map_err(|e| format!("--{}: {}", name, e)),
            None => Ok(None),
        }
    }
}
```

## `src/tap/engine/structs.rs`

```rust
use crate::argsparsing::ArgsP;
use std::{collections::HashMap, rc::Rc};

pub type ErrorType = Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;

pub type RawHandlerType = dyn Fn(&mut Engine<'_>, &[&str]) -> ErrorType;
pub type HandlerType = Rc<RawHandlerType>;
pub type SubHandlerType = fn(&[&str]) -> ErrorType;

pub type CmdInfoCmd<'a> = CmdInfo<'a, HandlerType>;
pub type CmdInfoSubcmd<'a> = CmdInfo<'a, SubHandlerType>;

#[derive(PartialEq, Clone)]
pub struct CmdInfo<'a, H> {
    pub handler: H,
    pub required: Vec<&'a str>,
    pub optional: Vec<&'a str>,
    pub unlimited: bool,
    pub docs: &'static str,
}

pub type CmdMap<'a> = HashMap<&'a str, CmdInfoCmd<'a>>;
pub type SubCmdsMap<'a> = HashMap<&'a str, CmdInfoSubcmd<'a>>;
pub type BasicHandler<'a> = Option<CmdInfo<'a, HandlerType>>;

pub struct Engine<'a> {
    pub args_p: &'a mut ArgsP,
    pub cmds: CmdMap<'a>,
    pub subcmds: SubCmdsMap<'a>,
    pub basic_handler: BasicHandler<'a>,
    pub about: String,
}
```

## `examples/demo.rs`

```rust
//! Tap demo — the main library features in one small CLI.
//!
//! Try:
//!     cargo run --example demo -- help
//!     cargo run --example demo -- version
//!     cargo run --example demo -- greet Rust
//!     cargo run --example demo -- greet --loud Rust
//!     cargo run --example demo -- add 2 3.5
//!     cargo run --example demo -- serve 127.0.0.1 8080 --verbose --tls=on --workers=8
//!     cargo run --example demo -- report
//!     cargo run --example demo -- echo hello world

use tap::{
    argsparsing::ArgsP,
    args, commands, cprintln, ensure, scope, subcommands, template, template_colored,
    engine::structs::{Engine, ErrorType},
    tooling::{add_help_handler, renderable::Renderable},
};

// ── Handlers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// `greet [name] [--loud]` — friendly greeting.
fn greet_handler(e: &mut Engine, raw: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    args! { raw;
        name: String = "World".to_string(),
    }
    cprintln!("[?BGN]Hello, [?YW]{}[?BGN]![?RT]", name);
    if e.flag("loud") {
        cprintln!("[?BD][?RD]>>> LOUD MODE ON <<<[?RT]");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `add <a> <b>` — typed parsing with helpful errors on bad input.
fn add_handler(_: &mut Engine, raw: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    args! { raw;
        a: f64,
        b: f64,
    }
    cprintln!("[?GN]{} + {} = [?BGN]{}[?RT]", a, b, a + b);
    Ok(())
}

/// `serve [host] [port] [--verbose] [--tls=on|off|auto] [--workers=N]`
fn serve_handler(e: &mut Engine, raw: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    args! { raw;
        host: String = "127.0.0.1".to_string(),
        port: u16 = 8080,
    }
    ensure!(port > 0, "port must be positive (got {})", port);

    let verbose = e.flag("verbose");
    let tls = e.value("tls").unwrap_or("off");
    ensure!(
        matches!(tls, "on" | "off" | "auto"),
        "invalid --tls value {:?} (expected on|off|auto)",
        tls
    );
    let workers: u16 = e.value_t("workers")?.unwrap_or(4);
    ensure!(workers > 0, "--workers must be positive");

    cprintln!("[?YW]Starting server...[?RT]");
    cprintln!("  [?CN]host[?RT]    = {}", host);
    cprintln!("  [?CN]port[?RT]    = {}", port);
    cprintln!("  [?CN]tls[?RT]     = {}", tls);
    cprintln!("  [?CN]workers[?RT] = {}", workers);
    cprintln!("  [?CN]verbose[?RT] = {}", verbose);
    Ok(())
}

/// `report` — render templates and JSON via `tooling::renderable`.
fn report_handler(_: &mut Engine, _: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    let mut r = Renderable::new();
    scope!(r;
        "name"        => "Tap",
        "version:int" => "156",
        "stable:bool" => "true",
        "tag"         => "tap-rs",
    );
    template!(r, "plain", "Hello, {{name}} v{{version}} ({{tag}})");
    template_colored!(r, "colored", "[?BGN]Hello, {{name}} [?YW]v{{version}}[?RT]");

    cprintln!("[?DM]--- plain ---[?RT]");
    println!("{}", r.render_with("plain")?);
    cprintln!("[?DM]--- colored ---[?RT]");
    println!("{}", r.render_with("colored")?);
    cprintln!("[?DM]--- json ---[?RT]");
    println!("{}", r.render_json()?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `version` — command with no arguments.
fn version_handler(_: &mut Engine, _: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    cprintln!("[?BGN]tap-rs[?RT] v[?YW]1.6.1[?RT]");
    Ok(())
}

/// `echo ...` — subcommand: plain `fn(&[&str])`, no `Engine` access.
fn echo_handler(raw: &[&str]) -> ErrorType {
    ensure!(!raw.is_empty(), "nothing to echo");
    cprintln!("[?GN]echo:[?RT] {}", raw.join(" "));
    Ok(())
}

// ── Wiring ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn main() {
    let mut ap = ArgsP::new();
    let mut engine = Engine::new(&mut ap, "TAP DEMO — lightweight CLI parsing".to_string());

    commands! {
        engine;
        "greet"   => greet_handler   { optional: ["name"],         docs: "Greet someone. Flag: --loud" }
        "add"     => add_handler     { required: ["a", "b"],       docs: "Sum two numbers" }
        "serve"   => serve_handler   { optional: ["host", "port"], docs: "Start a server. Flags: --verbose, --tls=on|off|auto, --workers=N" }
        "report"  => report_handler  {                             docs: "Render templates and JSON" }
        "version" => version_handler {                             docs: "Print version" }
    }

    subcommands! {
        engine;
        "echo" | "say" => echo_handler {
            unlimited: true,
            docs: "Echo back all arguments (subcommand)."
        }
    }

    add_help_handler(vec!["help", "-h"], &mut engine);

    if let Err(e) = engine.main() {
        cprintln!("[?RD][error][?RT] {}", e);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}
```
